questions.question: What is "register" in language?
options: The level of formality in your language
The speed at which you speak
questions.explanation: Register is the level of formality, ranging from informal slang and texting to formal academic writing.

questions.question: What is "tone" in writing?
options: The attitude or feeling in the text, such as friendly or serious
How loud the text is read aloud
questions.explanation: Tone is the attitude conveyed in the writing — friendly, serious, humorous, persuasive or neutral — created by word choice and style.

questions.question: Which features signal a FORMAL register?
options: No contractions, sophisticated vocabulary and passive constructions
questions.explanation: Formal register avoids contractions and slang, and uses sophisticated vocabulary, passive voice and impersonal constructions.

questions.question: What is the formal upgrade of "try"?
questions.explanation: Formal alternatives: try → attempt/endeavour, get → obtain, show → demonstrate, help → assist.

questions.question: A student writes an exam essay in texting style with slang. Why is this a problem?
options: The register does not match the situation, which examiners assess
Texting style is too difficult to read
questions.explanation: Examiners look for the ability to adapt language to the situation — a formal essay requires formal register.
